etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English faucet, fawcett, from Old French fausset, of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Late Latin falsāre (“to falsify”) or from a diminutive of Latin faux, faucēs (“throat”). Alternatively, from Old Norse foss, fors (“waterfall”); if so, cognate with English force, foss.

definitions.definition: (Canada, US) An exposed plumbing fitting; a tap or spigot; a regulator for controlling the flow of a liquid from a reservoir.

quote.citation: 2020, Brandon Taylor, Real Life, Daunt Books Originals, page 80:
quote.text: Wallace beats his palm against the reluctant handle of the faucet until it gives way, and the water comes out too hard, too fast.

definitions.definition: (game development) One or several systems that inject currency into the game's economy, thus controlling or preventing inflation
